### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **111** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec227fc7b18dbaea7ea635677db39063fb803206`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **25** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec227fc7b18dbaea7ea635677db39063fb803206` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c7ae32cc3e7db49ee92a232d450c93a169c81474` — the merge of head `91ba6cfc0ed232aea0ec5b9b03c1e8abea50ceba` into base `ec227fc7b18dbaea7ea635677db39063fb803206`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c7ae32cc3e7db49ee92a232d450c93a169c81474 && git checkout c7ae32cc3e7db49ee92a232d450c93a169c81474
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ec227fc7b18dbaea7ea635677db39063fb803206 91ba6cfc0ed232aea0ec5b9b03c1e8abea50ceba && git checkout -B drift-repro ec227fc7b18dbaea7ea635677db39063fb803206 && git merge --no-ff 91ba6cfc0ed232aea0ec5b9b03c1e8abea50ceba

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec227fc7b18dbaea7ea635677db39063fb803206
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ec227fc7b18dbaea7ea635677db39063fb803206` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 full · REWORK (1 must-fix, small)** · Head-sha: `4e1b7624f1eb285744a846a388f051648ce57bc9` · card #34780 (`Part of #34780`) · read 2026-11-18T17:42Z

Net diff against merge base `ec227fc7b18`: 17 files, +1483 / -55. All of it is in `packages/qa/scenarios` plus one changeset. It adds `--modes door`: a client that holds only the app's MCP draft door builds the card, the runner publishes the drafts as a person would, and then grades the result as a scratch build is graded. It has a skills arm and a rules arm.

### Must-fix

- **M1. The changeset's first body line is `Clause-②: no`, not the summary.** Each of the 43 changesets on main opens its body with the title line and puts the `Clause-②` / `Metadata-protocol` lines after it. The changelog generator takes the first body line as the entry's line. As written, `@objectstack/scenarios`' CHANGELOG entry would read "Clause-②: no", and the `feat(scenarios): …` title would fall into its body. Move the title line first.

### Should-fix (does not block)

- **S1. A rules-arm transcript can carry rule text.** The record states the arm by ids and sha256, never a text, and that holds for the arm field. But the turn's transcript is recorded too, and a client may quote a rule it was given in its own words or tool inputs. Rule texts may be the maintainer's private material, and eval-run records are filed publicly. One README line under the rules arm would cover it: read a rules-arm record before filing it anywhere public.

### Against the card

- **`Part of` is right.** The card is done when one round at five reps per arm is on record as an `eval-run`. That round needs a live model, so it is a maintainer action after merge, and the README gives the command.
- **Scope.** Both arms are present: with and without skills (`--door-skills` less `--door-skill-omit`), and with and without a named set of rule texts (`--door-rules` less `--door-rules-omit`). The build-skill arm itself waits on #34778, as the body says.
- **No hosted rule text is in the diff.** The rules arm reads a maintainer-supplied file at run time, a file inside the checkout is refused, and every fixture text is invented.

### Read at the head

- **The client holds the door and nothing else.**
  - The door turn runs in a fresh empty directory outside the host, which is removed after the turn.
  - It gets `--strict-mcp-config` with the one `app` server. `--allowedTools` is `mcp__app` (plus `Skill` when given skills), and `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write` and `NotebookEdit` are denied.
  - The token is in a 0600 config file in its own temp directory, also removed. It never appears on argv. The record keeps the token step's answer and scope, never the token.
- **Person-equivalent steps.**
  - Before the turn, the runner creates the package, then mints an OAuth 2.1 + PKCE token scoped `openid metadata:write`.
  - After the turn, it lists the drafts, then publishes them. Only a whole `published` with no `failed[]` counts as clean, since a refusal can answer on a 200. The ablation in the body pins that clause through the `published_unregistered` case.
  - Each refused step is a finding naming the step, and nothing that needed it runs. A harness without the four doors is a skip that names them.
- **Arms.**
  - The rules reader is a strict schema. It refuses each malformed input by name before any card runs, and it refuses a selector that omits every rule.
  - `summary` adds `door arm` as a table dimension, so two arms never sum into one cell.
  - Codex and external drivers are refused for door mode.
- **Replay.** A door turn's recorded `save_metadata_draft` / `delete_metadata_draft` calls are re-sent through the replay's own door and token, by the existing faithful-replay rule. Recorded MCP names are stripped of their `mcp__app__` prefix, so they match `DOOR_WRITE_TOOLS`.
- **Clause-② and metadata-protocol.** `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right for an eval-runner mode: no product package, no protocol and no authorable surface moves. No L2 is owed on that face.
- **Merges** cleanly onto origin/main `ec227fc7b1`.
- **Check-runs at this head:** 46 so far. None failed, and 13 are still running. I'll read them at the fixed head.

### Owed after the fix

- A delta L1 at the fixed head, once CI is green.
- Landing, through the seat. After merge, the five-reps round is the maintainer's.
